facts.text: Clifton earned its name from the natural cliffs overlooking Brownsboro Road, a feature highlighted by Colonel Bowles’ 1842 Italianate mansion.
The neighborhood’s streets follow the path of the 1830s Louisville and Shelbyville Turnpike, now Frankfort Avenue, which sparked early commerce.
During the Civil War, Clifton hosted Fort Elstner, a Union earthwork that never saw battle because Louisville stayed under Union control.
After a 1974 tornado, the Clifton Community Council revived the area, turning historic storefronts into restaurants, shops, and galleries.
Clifton’s historic district, listed on the National Register in 1983 and expanded in 1994, showcases Folk Victorian, Italianate, Queen Anne, and bungalow architecture.
Bingham Park, a local green space, offers biking trails and hosts community events that celebrate Clifton’s artistic heritage.
